2.title: 📦 Overview
2.content: 📖 📚🌐 Live Complete Documentation — Architecture guides, per-handler API reference, and testing instructions . hf-core is the shared platform layer for all HardFOC boards. It provides the handler layer, RTOS utilities, and driver integration that form the backbone of the HardFOC motor control system. hf-core is the bridge layer between hardware-agnostic base interfaces (BaseI2c, BaseSpi, BaseGpio, BaseAdc, BaseTemperature) and CRTP-templated device drivers (hf-tmc9660-driver, hf-bno08x-driver, hf-as5047u-driver, etc.). No board-specific configuration lives here — board HALs (e.g. hf-hal-vortex-v1) depend on this repo and add managers, API, and pin mapping.

37.title: HardFOC Flux V1 – Hardware Abstraction Layer
37.content: # HardFOC Flux V1 – Hardware Abstraction Layer ESP32 HAL for the **HardFOC Flux V1** valve-control board. Drives solenoid valves (MAX22200) and proportional valves (TLE92466ED) through a unified, stack-based manager architecture. ## Engineering handbook Cross-HAL **coding standards, architecture, CMake contract, testing, and agent playbooks** live in the [hf-development-handbook](https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-development-handbook) Git submodule at [`docs/hf-development-handbook/`](docs/hf-development-handbook/). After clone, run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. Start from [`docs/hf-development-handbook/README.md`](docs/hf-development-handbook/README.md). **Flux HAL doc hub (this repo):** [`docs/hal/README.md`](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/docs/hal/README.html) — architecture, manager map, and links to [`examples/esp32/docs/README.md`](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/examples/esp32/docs/README.html) for every `APP_TYPE`. Short index: [`DOCUMENTATION_INDEX.md`](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/DOCUMENTATION_INDEX.html). --- ## Board Overview | Feature | Detail |------------------------|--------------------------------------------------| **MCU** | ESP32 | **Solenoid Driver** | MAX22200 – 8-channel octal serial-controlled | **Proportional Driver**| TLE92466ED – 6-channel low-side switch | **Status LED** | WS2812 (NeoPixel), 1 LED, RMT channel 0 | **Temperature** | 10 kΩ NTC thermistor (B=3950) + ESP32 internal | **Voltage Monitor** | VBUS via 11× resistor divider on ADC1_CH0 | **Communication** | CAN/TWAI (500 kbps), I²C (400 kHz), SPI2 host | --- ## Pin Map ### SPI Bus (SPI2 – shared) | Signal | GPIO |--------|------| MOSI | 6 | MISO | 7 | SCLK | 2 | ### MAX22200 (Solenoid Driver) | Signal | GPIO |---------|------| CS | 18 | ENABLE | 11 | CMD | 10 | FAULT_N | 5 | ### TLE92466ED (Proportional Driver) | Signal | GPIO |---------|------| CS | 19 | RESN | 16 | EN | 17 | FAULT_N | 8 | ### CAN / TWAI | Signal | GPIO |--------|------| TX | 14 | RX | 15 | ### I²C | Signal | GPIO |--------|------| SDA | 21 | SCL | 22 | ### Analog | Channel | GPIO | ADC | Divider |--------------------|------|-----------|---------| NTC Thermistor | 4 | ADC1_CH4 | 1.0× | VBUS Monitor | 0 | ADC1_CH0 | 11.0× | ### LED | Signal | GPIO |---------|------| WS2812 | 3 | --- ## Architecture ``` ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Flux API │ Unified singleton entry point │ (Flux.h / Flux.cpp) │ ├──────────┬──────────┬──────────┬─────────────┤ │ CommChan │ GpioMgr │ ValveMgr │ AdcMgr │ │ Manager │ │ │ │ Managers │ │ │ │ LedMgr │ │ │ │ │ TempMgr │ ├──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴─────────────┤ │ Handler Layer (core) │ Max22200Handler, Tle92466edHandler, │ │ NtcTemperatureHandler, WS2812, Logger ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ Interface Wrappers (core) │ EspSpi, EspI2c, EspGpio, EspAdc, EspCan, │ │ EspTemperature, EspNvs, EspLogger └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### Design Principles - **Stack-based allocations** – Fixed-size `std::array` registries, `constexpr` mapping tables, linear scans for small-N lookups. Heap allocation only where ESP-IDF driver APIs require it (handler construction, WS2812 RMT buffer). - **Singleton managers** – Each manager is a Meyers singleton, initialized lazily on first access through `Flux::EnsureInitialized()`. - **CRTP SPI adapters** – External driver handlers use the Curiously Recurring Template Pattern for zero-overhead polymorphism. - **X-MACRO pin config** – All pin/ADC definitions live in `hf_functional_pin_config_flux_v1.hpp`, auto-generating enums, string tables, and mapping arrays. - **Shared `core/` submodule** – Handlers, interface wrappers, and utilities are symlinked from the Vortex HAL's core. --- ## Managers ### CommChannelsManager Initialises the shared SPI2 bus with two devices (MAX22200 @ Mode 0/10 MHz, TLE92466ED @ Mode 1/5 MHz) and CAN/TWAI at 500 kbps. Provides lazy `AcquireUart()` for serial sensors (BASIS-2, FDO2). Also exposes an opt-in `AcquireUsbSerialJtag()` accessor for the ESP32-S3 native-USB CDC-ACM/JTAG console — gated by the CMake flag `HF_CORE_ENABLE_USB_SERIAL_JTAG` (OFF by default; returns `nullptr` when disabled). Authoritative API: [`lib/managers/CommChannelsManager.h`](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/lib/managers/CommChannelsManager.h); see also [`docs/hal/managers-and-handlers.md`](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/docs/hal/managers-and-handlers.html). ### GpioManager Manages ESP32 GPIOs only (no I/O expander). Reads pin definitions from the X-MACRO pin config and registers GPIO + USER category pins. Provides name-based and enum-based access. ### ValveManager Unified interface to both valve drivers: - **Solenoid channels** (`SOL_CH0`–`SOL_CH7`): MAX22200 enable/disable, CDR/VDR current configuration, chopping frequency. - **Proportional channels** (`PROP_CH0`–`PROP_CH5`): TLE92466ED current setpoint (mA), PWM frequency, soft-start. - Fault detection, channel diagnostics, combined status reporting. ### AdcManager Two-channel ESP32 ADC1 manager: - NTC thermistor raw/voltage readings (voltage divider = 1.0×) - VBUS monitor with 11× divider compensation ### LedManager WS2812 LED with animation engine: - Solid, blink, breathe, rainbow animations - Status indicators: boot (blue blink), ready (green), warning (yellow blink), error (red fast-blink), calibrating (cyan breathe) ### TemperatureManager Dual-source temperature monitoring: - ESP32 internal die sensor - NTC thermistor via ADC, using `NtcTemperatureHandler` (10 kΩ, B=3950, 10 kΩ pull-up) - `GetSystemTemperatureStats()` for aggregate min/max/average --- ## API Changes (v2.0.0) | Area | Change |------|--------| **Diagnostics types** | `FluxAdcDiagnostics` → `AdcSystemDiagnostics`, `FluxTempDiagnostics` → `TempSystemDiagnostics` | **Return types** | `GetSystemDiagnostics()` returns typed error codes (`hf_adc_err_t`, `hf_valve_err_t`, `hf_gpio_err_t`) instead of `bool` | **Temperature** | `ReadTemperatureCelsius()` etc. return `TemperatureError` instead of `bool` | **Error tracking** | All managers now expose `GetLastError()` | **GPIO diagnostics** | New `GpioSystemDiagnostics` struct with interrupt counting | **GPIO interrupts** | `EnableInterrupt()`, `DisableInterrupt()`, `RegisterInterruptCallback()`, `GetInterruptCount()` | **Lifecycle** | `Flux::Shutdown()` for graceful reverse-order teardown | **Convenience** | `GetFlux()` free function (equivalent to `Flux::GetInstance()`), `GetCommChannelsManager()` | --- ## Quick Start ```cpp #include "api/Flux.h" void app_main() { auto& flux = hf::hal::flux::GetFlux(); flux.EnsureInitialized(); // Enable solenoid channel 0 flux.valves.EnableChannel(ValveManager::ValveChannel::SOL_CH0); // Set proportional valve current flux.valves.SetProportionalCurrent( ValveManager::ValveChannel::PROP_CH0, 500); // 500 mA // Read board temperature float temp = 0.0f; flux.temp.ReadTemperatureCelsius("NTC_THERMISTOR", temp); // Set LED to solid green flux.leds.SetAnimation(LedManager::LedAnimation::SOLID, {0, 255, 0}); // Print system info flux.DumpSystemStatistics(); } ``` --- ## Build This component is designed for the ESP-IDF build system (v5.0+). Add it to your project's `components/` directory or reference it via `EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS`: ```cmake set(EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS "/path/to/hf-all-hals/hf-hal-flux-v1" ) ``` Target: `esp32c6` ```bash idf.py set-target esp32c6 idf.py build ``` --- ## Directory Structure ``` hf-hal-flux-v1/ ├── CMakeLists.txt # ESP-IDF component build ├── idf_component.yml # Component manifest ├── README.md # This file ├── LICENSE ├── lib/ │ ├── api/ │ │ ├── Flux.h # Unified API singleton │ │ ├── Flux.cpp │ │ └── FluxVersion.h # Version constants │ ├── managers/ │ │ ├── CommChannelsManager.h/.cpp │ │ ├── GpioManager.h/.cpp │ │ ├── ValveManager.h/.cpp │ │ ├── AdcManager.h/.cpp │ │ ├── LedManager.h/.cpp │ │ └── TemperatureManager.h/.cpp │ └── core/ -> ../../hf-hal-vortex-v1/lib/core (symlink) │ ├── handlers/ # Max22200, Tle92466ed, NTC, WS2812, Logger │ ├── hf-core-drivers/ # ESP32 interface wrappers + external drivers │ └── hf-core-utils/ # RTOS wrappers, CAN utils, general utilities ``` --- ## License See [LICENSE](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/LICENSE).

41.title: Flux HAL — architecture (as implemented)
41.content: # Flux HAL — architecture (as implemented) ## Layers Same layered story as the handbook ([layered architecture](../hf-development-handbook/process/layered-architecture.md)): **Flux** → **HAL managers** → **`hf-core` handlers** → **drivers** → **`Base*`** → ESP-IDF. ## `Flux` members See **`lib/api/Flux.h`** for the full API. Subsystem references: | Member | Manager | Role |--------|---------|------| `nvs` | `NvsManager` | Namespaces for cal/config | `comms` | `CommChannelsManager` | SPI (valve drivers), CAN, UART pool | `gpio` | `GpioManager` | ESP32 GPIO | `valves` | `ValveManager` | MAX22200 + TLE92466ED paths | `adc` | `AdcManager` | ESP32 ADC (NTC, VBUS, … per board) | `leds` | `LedManager` | WS2812 status | `temp` | `TemperatureManager` | NTC + internal die / derived | ## Initialization (`Flux::InitializeAllComponents` in `lib/api/Flux.cpp`) Steps run in order with explicit **fatal** vs **non-fatal** behaviour: 1. **NvsManager** — **fatal** on failure (aborts whole init). 2. **CommChannelsManager** — **fatal**. 3. **GpioManager** — **fatal**. 4. **ValveManager** — **non-fatal** (logged; init sequence continues). 5. **AdcManager** — **non-fatal**. 6. **LedManager** — **non-fatal**. 7. **TemperatureManager** — **non-fatal**. So `EnsureInitialized()` returns **false** only when **NVS, comms, or GPIO** fails. Downstream subsystem failures still leave `EnsureInitialized()` **true** but with failed-component / warning lists — treat logs and `GetSystemDiagnostics()` as source of truth. `Shutdown()` reverses the stack (see `Flux.cpp`). ## CPU affinity Logical CPU indices for tasks are documented in **`lib/api/FluxCpuAffinity.h`** and referenced from `Flux.h`. ## Deeper reading | Topic | Where |--------|--------| Valve + pressure demo | [`examples/esp32/main/manifold_valves_pressure_control/README.md`](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/examples/esp32/main/manifold_valves_pressure_control/README.html) | Example app index | [`examples/esp32/docs/README.md`](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/examples/esp32/docs/README.html) |

45.title: Manifold valves & pressure sensor application
45.content: # Manifold valves & pressure sensor application This example is the WH bench-test acquisition + actuation stack. It owns: - **8 Honeywell SSC TruStability** ratiometric pressure transducers on the ADS7952 12-bit SPI ADC. - **7 Parker C15 / C21 / SRS / VSO** valves driven through the **MAX22200** octal solenoid driver (6 binary hit/hold + 1 pseudo-proportional). - **6 Parker VSO / VSO MaxFlow / LM-Pro** precision proportional valves driven through the **TLE92466ED** 6-channel current-controlled driver. A boot-time **valve self-test** exercises every catalog entry one at a time (solenoids ON/OFF, proportionals 0 → full → 0) and reports per-channel faults from the underlying drivers — see §6. Everything hangs off the existing Flux V1 HAL — this folder contributes the **application-level abstractions** (named valves, datasheet-driven profiles, lock-free positional API, dedicated control + diagnostics threads, full per-driver fault decoding). --- ## 1. Architecture overview ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Application / control-loop threads (any rate) │ │ - PressureSensor::GetPressureFiltered() lock-free atomic │ │ - ManifoldValves::Get(SolenoidId).RequestState/RequestPosition │ │ - ManifoldValves::Get(ProportionalId).RequestPosition │ │ - .GetActualPosition() / .GetState() / .Snapshot() lock-free │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ PressureSensorThread (1 kHz) │ │ ManifoldValvesControlThread (100 Hz)│ │ - Auto-1 batched ADS7952 │ │ - ConsumeDirty() per valve │ │ - Per-channel single-pole │ │ - Apply() → ValveManager │ │ IIR + atomic publish │ │ - Updates actual_position │ └──────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread (10 Hz) │ │ - Per-valve OnDiagnostics() → per-channel snapshot │ │ - MAX22200 STATUS register → SubsystemFaultSnapshot.max_* │ │ - TLE92466 FaultReport → SubsystemFaultSnapshot.tle_* │ │ - Aggregates lock-free SubsystemFaultSnapshot for the app │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Flux::ValveManager + Flux::AdcManager + Flux::CommChannels │ │ - MAX22200 (SOL_CH0..SOL_CH5) ← all 6 solenoids │ │ - TLE92466ED (PROP_CH0..PROP_CH5) ← all 6 precision proportionals │ │ - ADS7952 (SPI3) ← pressure ADC │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### 1.1 Why three threads? | Thread | Period | Job |--------|--------|-----| Pressure sampling | 1 ms | Match the SSC ASIC's 1 kHz pressure update; produce filtered atomic snapshots that any control loop can consume lock-free. | Valve control | 10 ms | Push every dirty valve setpoint to MAX22200 / TLE92466ED. Doing this at 100 Hz keeps SPI traffic low while still feeling instant to a 500 Hz outer control loop. | Diagnostics | 100 ms | Read per-channel + global driver-IC fault registers and surface a comprehensive `SubsystemFaultSnapshot` so the application doesn't ever have to do multi-register SPI reads itself. | This separation means the control loop **never** has to read fault registers itself — that's the diagnostics thread's responsibility — and the diagnostics thread **never** delays the application's set/get path. --- ## 2. Pressure sensors Honeywell SSC TruStability sensors output **10 % – 90 % of V_supply** over the configured pressure range (transfer function "A"), with output clipping limits at 2.5 % / 97.5 %. Resolution ≥ 0.03 % FSS, accuracy ±0.25 % FSS BFSL, total error band ±2 % FSS, ASIC update ≈ 1 kHz, response ≈ 1 ms. Bench wiring: | Channel | Label | Range | Direction |---------|----------|------------------|------------| CH0 | DPS_LOW | ±0.18 PSI | Differential | CH1 | DPS_HIGH | ±2.32 PSI | Differential | CH2 | PMS | 0 – 5 PSI | Positive | CH3 | PLS_LOW | 0 – 15 PSI | Positive | CH4 | PLS_HIGH | 0 – 150 PSI | Positive | CH5 | RLS | 0 → -30 PSI | Negative (vacuum) | CH6 | PWS2 | 0 – 1 PSI | Positive | CH7 | PWS1 | 0 – 1 PSI | Positive | Pipeline: 1 kHz Auto-1 batched ADS7952 read → per-channel single-pole IIR LPF (default fc = 100 Hz at fs = 1 kHz) → atomic publish. Lock-free `PressureSensor::GetPressureFiltered()` for control loops. --- ## 3. Valves ### 3.1 Driver-IC capabilities (what we expose) #### MAX22200 (octal solenoid driver, 8 channels — using 6) | Capability | Use here |------------|----------| **CDR (Current Drive Regulation)** — 7-bit current ladder per channel | Hit & hold currents on every BinaryHitHold solenoid; sustained current on the SEV pseudo-proportional. | **VDR (Voltage / PWM Duty Regulation)** | Available via `ValveManager::ConfigureSolenoidVdr` — not used today. | **Per-channel feature gates** (CFG_CH register) | All four exposed via `Max22200ChannelFeatures`: `slew_rate_control` (cleaner edges, lower EMI), `open_load_detection`, `plunger_movement_detection`, `hit_current_check`. | **DPM (Detection of Plunger Movement)** — global algorithm (CFG_DPM) | `ManifoldValves::ConfigureGlobalDpm(start_ma, dip_ma, debounce_ms)` configures ISTART / IPTH / TDEB. Per-channel DPM_EN bits set from the catalog's feature gate. | **Per-channel faults** (FAULT register) | `SolenoidValve::Snapshot()` returns `overcurrent`, `hit_not_reached`, `open_load`, `plunger_movement_fault` plus sticky counters. | **Global health** (STATUS register) | `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread::SubsystemFaultSnapshot.max_*` carries OVT, COMER, UVM, the global OCP/OLF/HHF/DPM bits and the active-channels mask. | #### TLE92466ED (six-channel current-controlled, 6 channels — using all 6) | Capability | Use here |------------|----------| **Closed-loop current control** | `ValveManager::SetProportionalCurrent` per valve, called every dirty Apply. | **PWM frequency** (mantissa+exponent encoded) | Each valve's `pwm_hz` from the model spec is pushed once via `ValveManager::ConfigureProportionalPwm`. | **Dither** (step size + steps + flat period) | Pushed once via `ValveManager::ConfigureProportionalDither` for VSO-class valves. LM-Pro skips dither (it's a linear motor). | **Slew rate / diagnostic current / open-load threshold / OLSG warning** | Configured via `tle92466ed::ChannelConfig` from `Tle92466ChannelFeatures`. | **Per-channel diagnostics** | `ProportionalValve::Snapshot()` carries every flag from `tle92466ed::ChannelDiagnostics`: `overcurrent`, `short_to_ground`, `open_load`, `over_temperature`, `open_load_short_ground`, `ot_warning`, `current_regulation_warning`, `pwm_regulation_warning`, `olsg_warning`, plus live measurements `average_current_raw`, `duty_cycle_raw`, `vbat_feedback_raw`. | **Global health** (FaultReport) | `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread::SubsystemFaultSnapshot.tle_*` carries VBAT/VIO/VDD UV/OV, central OT warning/error, clock fault, SPI watchdog, POR/reset events, register/OTP ECC errors, supply-NOK summaries. | ### 3.2 Bench mapping **Solenoids (MAX22200, channels 0–7):** | OUTn | ID | Drive mode | Model | Datasheet currents (24 V) |------------|-------|---------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------| SOL_CH0 | _spare_ | _unconnected_ | — | — | SOL_CH1 | OLV_2 | BinaryHitHold | Parker C21 (R = 235 Ω) | hit 102 mA / hold 51 mA / hit 100 ms | SOL_CH2 | VEV | BinaryHitHold | Parker C15 ≥0.040″ (R = 361 Ω) | hit 66 mA / hold 33 mA / hit 100 ms | SOL_CH3 | OLV_1 | BinaryHitHold | Parker C21 | same as OLV_2 | **SOL_CH4** | **SEV** | **VariableCurrent** | **Parker VSO (R = 274 Ω)** | **0..66 mA proportional via 7-bit CDR ladder** | SOL_CH5 | GDV | BinaryHitHold | Parker SRS 0.5 W (R = 1152 Ω) | hit 21 mA / hold 10 mA / hit 30 ms | SOL_CH6 | ORV | BinaryHitHold | Parker C15 ≥0.040″ | hit 66 mA / hold 33 mA / hit 100 ms | SOL_CH7 | AVV | BinaryHitHold | Parker C15 ≥0.040″ | same as ORV | **Proportionals (TLE92466ED, channels 0–5):** > The TLE92466ED PWM frequency is capped at 4 kHz by the chip itself (datasheet > `PERIOD::kSpecMaxFrequency`). The catalog therefore drives every model at > 4 kHz; the driver clamps and warns if you ever request more. LM-Pro keeps a > tiny "telemetry" dither (1 mA @ 50 Hz) so the chip's `FB_I_AVG` / `FB_DC` > averagers are populated — see `hf-tle92466ed-driver/docs/troubleshooting.md`. | OUTn | ID | Model | Full-flow current | PWM | Dither |-----------|-------|-----------------------------|-------------------|---------|----------------------| PROP_CH0 | FRV | Parker VSO MaxFlow 24 V | 66 mA | 4 kHz | 4 mA @ 200 Hz | PROP_CH1 | SPV_L | Parker VSO 24 V | 66 mA | 4 kHz | 4 mA @ 200 Hz | PROP_CH2 | FCV | Parker VSO MaxFlow 24 V | 66 mA | 4 kHz | 4 mA @ 200 Hz | PROP_CH3 | LSV | Parker VSO MaxFlow 24 V | 66 mA | 4 kHz | 4 mA @ 200 Hz | PROP_CH4 | SPV_H | Parker LM-Pro 24 V | 115 mA | 4 kHz | 1 mA @ 50 Hz (telemetry) | PROP_CH5 | GFV | Parker LM-Pro 24 V | 115 mA | 4 kHz | 1 mA @ 50 Hz (telemetry) | ### 3.3 SEV — pseudo-proportional via MAX22200 SEV is a Parker VSO proportional valve, but because precise control is not required at this site we route it through MAX22200 instead of taking up a TLE92466ED channel. The driver mode is `VariableCurrent`: - Every Apply() pushes `ConfigureSolenoidCdr(target_ma, target_ma, hit_time = 0)`. - With `hit_time = 0` the MAX22200 skips the hit phase; the channel runs at a steady current equal to the requested setpoint. - Resolution is 7-bit (≈ 128 steps over 0..IFS); for SEV's 0..66 mA range that's ~0.5 mA per step — more than enough for opening-percentage control. - DPM and HHF are disabled for SEV (no hit phase to check; the dip signature DPM looks for is for binary on/off solenoids). ### 3.4 Per-valve atomic state (`Valve.h`) Every valve carries: ```text target_pos_ atomic — last setpoint requested (0..1) target_dirty_ atomic — pending application? actual_pos_ atomic — last position the control thread set state_ atomic— Idle / Active / Faulted / … last_error_ atomic apply_count_ atomic apply_error_count_ atomic fault_count_ atomic last_fault_tick_ms_ atomic ``` All `Get*` accessors use `memory_order_acquire`; the control / diagnostics threads use `memory_order_release` on their writes. A single load yields a self-consistent snapshot — control loops never need a mutex. ### 3.5 Application API ```cpp auto& sys = manifold_valves::ManifoldValves::GetInstance(); // Binary solenoid: sys.Get(manifold_valves::SolenoidId::OLV_1).RequestState(true); bool actual_on = sys.Get(manifold_valves::SolenoidId::OLV_1).IsActuallyEnergised(); // Pseudo-proportional solenoid (SEV via MAX22200 CDR): sys.Get(manifold_valves::SolenoidId::SEV).RequestPosition(0.42f); // 0..1 // Precision proportional (TLE92466ED): sys.Get(manifold_valves::ProportionalId::FCV).RequestPosition(0.42f); float actual = sys.Get(manifold_valves::ProportionalId::FCV).GetActualPosition(); // Per-valve diagnostic snapshot: auto sol_snap = sys.Get(manifold_valves::SolenoidId::OLV_1).Snapshot(); if (sol_snap.plunger_movement_fault) { /* handle stuck valve */ } auto pro_snap = sys.Get(manifold_valves::ProportionalId::FCV).Snapshot(); uint16_t avg_current = pro_snap.average_current_raw; // live measured // Subsystem-wide health (run by ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread): auto sub = valve_diag.GetSnapshot(); if (sub.tle_vbat_uv || sub.max_undervoltage) { /* supply problem */ } ``` All `Request*` and `Get*` calls are lock-free. The actual SPI traffic happens on the next iteration of the control / diagnostics threads. --- ## 4. Diagnostics for medical-device safety The diagnostics thread surfaces every flag the chip can publish — not just "any fault" booleans. This is what allows the application layer to make informed safety decisions: ### 4.1 Active diagnostics — react in software | Signal | Meaning | Recommended response |--------|---------|----------------------| `Solenoid.plunger_movement_fault` | Plunger did not move under load | Mark valve mechanically stuck; alarm; safe-state the system. | `Solenoid.hit_not_reached` | HIT current never achieved within tHIT | Coil drift, supply sag or open coil. Re-attempt; alarm if persistent. | `Solenoid.open_load` | No load current path | Disconnected coil or wire. Disable channel, alarm. | `Solenoid.overcurrent` | Short to supply or shorted coil | Disable immediately; latch. | `Proportional.short_to_ground` | Short to ground | Latched fault. | `Proportional.over_temperature` | Channel die over-temp | Reduce setpoint; back-off duty; alarm. | `Proportional.current_regulation_warning` | Loop can't track current setpoint | Investigate wiring, supply, dither tuning. | `Subsystem.tle_vbat_uv` / `_ov` | Supply rail UV/OV | Stop actuating; raise system alarm. | `Subsystem.tle_spi_wd_error` | SPI watchdog tripped | Communication is failing; latch and re-init. | `Subsystem.tle_reg_ecc_err` / `tle_otp_ecc_err` | Register / OTP memory error | Treat as hard failure; latch. | `Subsystem.max_undervoltage` (UVM) | MAX22200 supply UV at boot or runtime | Re-read STATUS at init clears it; runtime UV is an alarm. | `Subsystem.max_communication_error` | SPI error detected by MAX22200 | Re-init; alarm if persistent. | ### 4.2 Preventive features (configured at startup) - **Slew-rate control** enabled by default on every solenoid → cleaner switching edges, lower EMI, less acoustic clicking. - **Open-load detection** enabled on every channel → catches a disconnected coil before it hides a real safety event. - **Hit-current check (HHF)** enabled on every binary solenoid → if the hit current isn't reached within tHIT we know the solenoid never energised. - **DPM (plunger movement)** enabled on all 5 binary cartridge solenoids. Tuned via `ConfigureGlobalDpm(30 mA, 8 mA, 0.5 ms)` at boot — adjust per the actual mechanical signature. - **OLSG warning** on every TLE92466 channel → early indication of open-load / short-to-ground precursors. - **CRC + SPI watchdog + clock watchdog** on TLE92466ED globally (configured by `Flux::ValveManager` on init). --- ## 5. Failure / degraded-mode behaviour If `Flux::ValveManager` fails to bring up either driver IC (the WH bench in its current state shows exactly this — the hardware isn't connected): - `ValveManager::IsInitialized()` returns `false`. - `ManifoldValvesControlThread` keeps stepping but skips `Apply()` calls. - `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread` reports `manager_ready = false` and zeroes the per-driver readiness flags / fault snapshots. - All `Valve::Get*` accessors keep returning the last-published soft state (`Uninitialized` / 0 / `VALVE_SUCCESS`). This means an outer control loop can be developed and unit-tested against the same atomic API even when the valve hardware isn't wired up. --- ## 6. Boot self-test (`ManifoldValvesSelfTest`) Every boot, after the pressure thread is calibrated and the valve control + diagnostics threads are running, the application calls `ManifoldValvesSelfTest::Run()`. This single function: 1. **Walks every solenoid in the catalog** (`SolenoidId::OLV_2 → AVV`) and: - Prints a banner ("Connect ONLY SOL '' …") with a configurable prompt countdown so the operator can move the manifold tube. - Cycles the channel `solenoid_cycles` × (ON `solenoid_on_ms` / OFF `solenoid_off_ms`) — exact same test pattern as the `c21_cycle_test.cpp` example in the MAX22200 driver. - After each ON/OFF transition waits two full diagnostics-thread sweeps and logs a per-channel snapshot (`tgt`, `act`, state, OCP / HHF / OLF / DPM flags, sticky `fc`). 2. **Walks every proportional in the catalog** (`ProportionalId::FRV → GFV`) and: - Prompts the operator (same pattern). - Ramps `0 → full-flow → 0` in `proportional_steps` increments with a `proportional_settle_ms` settle between each setpoint — same pattern as the `lm_pro_cycle_test.cpp` example in the TLE92466ED driver. - Logs the chip's live telemetry at every step: commanded current, `FB_I_AVG` raw, `FB_DC` raw, `last_err`, every fault flag and every warning. 3. **Aggregates a per-valve PASS/FAIL** based on: - `apply_error_count_` delta (ANY non-success Apply during the cycle). - `fault_count_` delta (any per-channel fault flag set during the cycle). - The most recent diagnostic snapshot (`Snapshot::any_fault()`). The summary block at the end prints OK / FAIL plus a one-line fault description for each valve. ### 6.1 Operator workflow on a manifold-limited rig The bench can only mechanically attach **one valve to the manifold at a time**. The defaults (`prompt_wait_ms = 3000`, `inter_valve_pause_ms = 4000`) are tuned for that workflow: | Phase | Duration |---------------------------------|----------| Per-valve operator prompt | 3 s | Per-valve test (solenoid) | ~12 s (3 × on/off cycles) | Per-valve test (proportional) | ~5 s (22 ramp setpoints × 0.15 s) | Pause between valves | 4 s | **Full sweep** (7 sol + 6 prop) | **≈ 3 min** | Tweak the constants in `MakeSelfTestPlan()` at the top of `manifold_valves_pressure_control.cpp` to: - skip valves that are not yet stocked (set the `enable_*` flag to `false`); - shorten / lengthen the pulse profiles or ramp resolution; - disable the operator prompt (`prompt_wait_ms = 0`) for fully unattended runs. To skip the self-test entirely set `kRunSelfTestAtBoot = false` at the top of the same file. ### 6.2 What the self-test catches The self-test is the cheapest way to **catch a stuck plunger, an unconnected coil, a damaged driver IC, or an audibly dead solenoid** before the rig starts running pressure-control loops. Specifically: | Symptom | Catalog check that surfaces it |------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------| Coil disconnected / connector reversed | `open_load` / `open_load_short_ground` flag, `last_err = "Open load detected"` | Coil shorted to GND | `short_to_ground` flag (TLE92466ED) | Plunger stuck in valve seat | `plunger_movement_fault` (MAX22200 DPM) | Solenoid hit current never reached | `hit_not_reached` (MAX22200 HHF) | TLE chip not in correct mode | `last_err = "Operation not allowed in mode"` (Apply-time error count) | Supply browning out | `SubsystemFaultSnapshot.max_undervoltage` / `tle_vbat_uv` | TLE PWM regulation can't track | `pwm_regulation_warning` | TLE current loop can't track | `current_regulation_warning` | Over-temperature, ECC error | `over_temperature` / `ot_warning` / `tle_reg_ecc_err` | > ⚠️ **Configuration-Mode round-trip:** Each `ProportionalValve` enters > Configuration Mode, pushes its `ChannelConfig` + PWM + dither, then > re-enters Mission Mode. This is required because the TLE92466ED rejects > any `CH_x_CTRL` write while in Mission Mode and the handler enters > Mission Mode at init time. Skipping this round-trip is what produced the > infamous "every Apply returns Operation-not-allowed-in-mode" symptom. --- ## 7. Extension recipes ### 6.1 Add a binary solenoid 1. Add an enumerator in `manifold_valves::SolenoidId` before `Count`. 2. Append a row in `kSolenoidMap` referencing one of the `kSpec*` model structs and an unused `ValveChannel::SOL_CHn`. ### 6.2 Add a pseudo-proportional via MAX22200 Same as above, but: - pick `SolenoidDriveMode::VariableCurrent`, - use a model spec with `full_flow_current_ma` set and `hit_current_ma = hold_current_ma = 0`, - disable `plunger_movement_detection` and `hit_current_check` in the channel features (the current waveform in continuous-current mode is not what those algorithms were designed for). ### 6.3 Add a precision proportional 1. Add an enumerator in `manifold_valves::ProportionalId` before `Count` (TLE92466 has 6 channels — if you exceed that you need a second IC). 2. Append a row in `kProportionalMap` with the right model spec and feature gates. ### 6.4 Use a different model Edit (or add) a `SolenoidModelSpec` / `ProportionalModelSpec` literal at the top of `ManifoldValvesCatalog.h`, then point the relevant table row at it. Only the catalog file changes. ### 6.5 Re-tune diagnostics - DPM parameters: `ManifoldValves::ConfigureGlobalDpm(start, dip, debounce)`. Default 30 mA / 8 mA / 0.5 ms tuned for the C21 hold band; adjust per the actual mechanical signature. - Per-channel feature gates: edit the `Max22200ChannelFeatures` / `Tle92466ChannelFeatures` row in the bench map. - Diagnostics thread cadence: `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread::SetPeriodMs(n)` — default 100 ms, drop to 20 ms for closer monitoring or raise to 500 ms to lighten SPI load. --- ## 8. Files in this folder | File | Purpose |------|---------| `manifold_valves_pressure_control.cpp` | App entry: brings up Flux, calibrates pressure sensors, configures DPM, starts control + diagnostics threads. | `PressureSensorConfig.h` | Sensor enums + ratiometric range + calibration config types. | `PressureSensor.{h,cpp}` | Per-channel pressure sensor: IIR filter, atomic publish. | `PressureSensorThread.{h,cpp}` | 1 kHz BaseThread + Auto-1 ADS7952 batch read. | `ManifoldValvesCatalog.h` | Compile-time enums + Parker valve datasheet specs + bench map + per-channel diagnostic feature gates. | `Valve.h` | Base valve class (atomic state, dirty flag, snapshot types). | `SolenoidValve.h` | MAX22200-driven valve — handles BinaryHitHold and VariableCurrent modes; decodes per-channel OCP/HHF/OLF/DPM. | `ProportionalValve.h` | TLE92466ED-driven precision proportional; full per-channel ChannelDiagnostics surfacing. | `ManifoldValves.h` | Singleton container, O(1) lookup, iteration helpers, `ConfigureGlobalDpm`. | `ManifoldValvesControlThread.h` | 100 Hz BaseThread that pushes dirty setpoints. | `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread.h` | 10 Hz BaseThread; per-valve + per-driver-IC fault decoding into `SubsystemFaultSnapshot`. | `ManifoldValvesSelfTest.h` | Boot-time per-valve cycler — solenoid ON/OFF and proportional 0→full→0 ramps with full diagnostic capture. Header-only; configured from `MakeSelfTestPlan()` in the app entry. | `README.md` | This document. |

# Flux API — Unified HardFOC Platform Interface ## CPU affinity (`FluxCpuAffinity.h`) FreeRTOS task pinning uses **logical** core indices defined in `FluxCpuAffinity.h` (`flux_hal::kFluxCpuNoAffinity`, `kFluxCpuHostIo`, `kFluxCpuRealtime`). Application firmware (`main/`) includes that header only—vendor core names (e.g. PRO/APP on Espressif dual-core parts) are documented in the board integration guide, not as macros in `main/`. ## Overview The Flux API provides a unified singleton interface to all component managers in the HardFOC Flux V1 platform. It implements lazy initialization with proper dependency management, ensuring all subsystems are correctly initialized before exposing them to the application. ## Architecture ### Design Principles - **True Singleton Pattern**: Uses Meyer's singleton for thread-safe initialization - **Lazy Initialization**: Components are initialized only when needed - **Dependency Management**: Proper initialization order based on component dependencies - **Exception-Free Design**: All methods are `noexcept` with proper error handling - **Reference-Based Access**: Direct access to component managers by reference - **Comprehensive Diagnostics**: Full system health monitoring and diagnostics ### Component Dependencies The initialization order is carefully managed to handle dependencies: ``` 1. NvsManager (ESP-IDF NVS — `flux` / `flux_cal` / `flux_cfg` namespaces) ↓ 2. CommChannelsManager (SPI, CAN, lazy UART, opt-in USB Serial/JTAG — no I²C on Flux V1) ↓ 3. GpioManager (depends on comms for future expansion) ↓ 4. ValveManager (depends on comms + gpio for drivers) ↓ 5. AdcManager (ESP32 internal ADC, independent) ↓ 6. LedManager (WS2812, independent) ↓ 7. TemperatureManager (depends on ADC) ``` > **Logger backend.** `Flux::EnsureInitialized()` (and the constructor's > early `Logger::GetInstance().Initialize()` call) use the **default** > `Logger::Initialize(const LogConfig&)` overload, which delegates to the > per-MCU factory `Logger::CreateDefaultBaseLogger()`. On ESP32 builds > that factory lives in `hf-core/handlers/logger/factory/EspLoggerFactory.cpp` > and returns an `EspLogger` — so `Logger.cpp` itself never includes any > ESP-IDF headers. To inject a custom backend (e.g. one that writes over > `EspUsbSerialJtag` instead of UART0), call the second `Initialize` > overload **before** `Flux::EnsureInitialized()`. See the > [`Logger` handler README](../core/handlers/logger/README.md). ## Quick Start ### Basic Usage ```cpp #include "api/Flux.h" #include "core/hf-core-drivers/internal/hf-internal-interface-wrap/inc/base/BaseNvs.h" // Get the Flux API instance auto& flux = Flux::GetInstance(); // Ensure all systems are initialized if (flux.EnsureInitialized()) { // Non-volatile storage (BaseNvs — calibration, config, app keys) BaseNvs& cal = flux.nvs.Calibration(); (void)cal.KeyExists("my_cal_key"); // Access communication channels auto& comms = flux.comms; // Access GPIO management auto& gpio = flux.gpio; // Access valve control auto& valves = flux.valves; // Access ADC channels auto& adc = flux.adc; // Access LED management auto& leds = flux.leds; // Access temperature sensors auto& temp = flux.temp; } ``` ### String-Based Access (Convenience) ```cpp auto& flux = Flux::GetInstance(); if (flux.EnsureInitialized()) { // GPIO operations flux.gpio.Set("GPIO_MAX22200_FAULT", true); bool state; flux.gpio.Read("GPIO_TLE_DIAG", state); // ADC operations float voltage; flux.adc.ReadVoltage("ADC_NTC_THERM", voltage); // Valve control flux.valves.EnableChannel(ValveChannel::SOL_CH0); // LED status flux.leds.SetStatus(LedAnimation::STATUS_OK); } ``` ### Cached Access (High Performance) ```cpp auto& flux = Flux::GetInstance(); if (flux.EnsureInitialized()) { // Cache pointers for fast access (do once, outside loops) auto* adc_ntc = flux.adc.Get("ADC_NTC_THERM"); auto* adc_vbus = flux.adc.Get("ADC_VBUS_MONITOR"); if (!adc_ntc || !adc_vbus) { printf("ERROR: Failed to cache component pointers
"); return; } // Use cached pointers in high-frequency operations for (int i = 0; i ReadChannelV(0, ntc_v); adc_vbus->ReadChannelV(0, vbus_v); } } ``` ### Advanced Usage ```cpp // Get system diagnostics FluxSystemDiagnostics diagnostics; if (flux.GetSystemDiagnostics(diagnostics)) { printf("System Health: %s
", diagnostics.system_healthy ? "HEALTHY" : "UNHEALTHY"); printf("Initialized Components: %u/%u
", diagnostics.initialized_components, diagnostics.total_components); } // Collect per-manager health ManagerHealthSnapshot snapshot; if (flux.CollectManagerHealth(snapshot)) { for (size_t i = 0; i GetComponentInitializationStatus() const noexcept; size_t GetFailedComponents(const char* out[], size_t max_count) const noexcept; size_t GetSystemWarnings(const char* out[], size_t max_count) const noexcept; bool CollectManagerHealth(ManagerHealthSnapshot& snapshot) noexcept; ``` ### Utility Methods ```cpp uint64_t GetSystemUptimeMs() const noexcept; uint64_t GetInitializationTimeMs() const noexcept; void DumpSystemStatistics() const noexcept; bool PerformHealthCheck() noexcept; const char* GetSystemVersion() const noexcept; ``` ### Convenience Accessor ```cpp [[nodiscard]] inline Flux& GetFlux() noexcept; ``` Equivalent to `Flux::GetInstance()`. ### Macros ```cpp #define FLUX_API Flux::GetInstance() #define FLUX_API_INIT() (Flux::GetInstance().EnsureInitialized(), Flux::GetInstance()) ``` ## System Diagnostics ### FluxSystemDiagnostics ```cpp struct FluxSystemDiagnostics { bool system_healthy; bool nvs_initialized; bool comms_initialized; bool gpio_initialized; bool valves_initialized; bool adc_initialized; bool leds_initialized; bool temp_initialized; uint32_t total_components; // equals kFluxManagerCount (7) uint32_t initialized_components; uint32_t failed_components; uint64_t initialization_time_ms; uint64_t system_uptime_ms; const char* failed_components_list[kFluxManagerCount]; size_t failed_components_list_count; }; ``` ### ManagerHealthSnapshot ```cpp struct ManagerHealthSnapshot { ManagerHealthEntry entries[kFluxManagerCount]; size_t count; size_t managers_with_errors; bool all_healthy; }; ``` ## Performance ### Initialization Time - **Fast Path**: ~30–80 ms (all components healthy) - **Slow Path**: ~150–400 ms (with retries and error handling) ### Memory Usage - **Static Memory**: ~1.5 KB (singleton instance) - **Runtime Memory**: ~0.5 KB (diagnostics and state tracking) - **Component Memory**: Varies by component (not owned by API) ### Thread Safety - **Singleton Access**: Thread-safe (Meyer's singleton) - **Initialization**: Thread-safe with atomic operations - **Component Access**: Depends on individual component implementations ## NVS example (ESP32-S3) See `examples/esp32/main/flux_nvs_example.cpp` — build and flash with: `./scripts/build_app.sh flux_nvs_example Debug` then `./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor flux_nvs_example Debug` from `examples/esp32/`. ## Related documentation - [HAL documentation hub](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/docs/hal/README.html) - [Manager ↔ handler map](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/docs/hal/managers-and-handlers.html) - Manager headers: [`../../lib/managers/`](../../lib/managers/)

52.title: Manifold valves & pressure sensor application
52.content: # Manifold valves & pressure sensor application This example is the WH bench-test acquisition + actuation stack. It owns: - **8 Honeywell SSC TruStability** ratiometric pressure transducers on the ADS7952 12-bit SPI ADC. - **7 Parker C15 / C21 / SRS / VSO** valves driven through the **MAX22200** octal solenoid driver (6 binary hit/hold + 1 pseudo-proportional). - **6 Parker VSO / VSO MaxFlow / LM-Pro** precision proportional valves driven through the **TLE92466ED** 6-channel current-controlled driver. A boot-time **valve self-test** exercises every catalog entry one at a time (solenoids ON/OFF, proportionals 0 → full → 0) and reports per-channel faults from the underlying drivers — see §6. Everything hangs off the existing Flux V1 HAL — this folder contributes the **application-level abstractions** (named valves, datasheet-driven profiles, lock-free positional API, dedicated control + diagnostics threads, full per-driver fault decoding). --- ## 1. Architecture overview ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Application / control-loop threads (any rate) │ │ - PressureSensor::GetPressureFiltered() lock-free atomic │ │ - ManifoldValves::Get(SolenoidId).RequestState/RequestPosition │ │ - ManifoldValves::Get(ProportionalId).RequestPosition │ │ - .GetActualPosition() / .GetState() / .Snapshot() lock-free │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────────┐ │ PressureSensorThread (1 kHz) │ │ ManifoldValvesControlThread (100 Hz)│ │ - Auto-1 batched ADS7952 │ │ - ConsumeDirty() per valve │ │ - Per-channel single-pole │ │ - Apply() → ValveManager │ │ IIR + atomic publish │ │ - Updates actual_position │ └──────────────────────────────┘ └──────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread (10 Hz) │ │ - Per-valve OnDiagnostics() → per-channel snapshot │ │ - MAX22200 STATUS register → SubsystemFaultSnapshot.max_* │ │ - TLE92466 FaultReport → SubsystemFaultSnapshot.tle_* │ │ - Aggregates lock-free SubsystemFaultSnapshot for the app │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Flux::ValveManager + Flux::AdcManager + Flux::CommChannels │ │ - MAX22200 (SOL_CH0..SOL_CH5) ← all 6 solenoids │ │ - TLE92466ED (PROP_CH0..PROP_CH5) ← all 6 precision proportionals │ │ - ADS7952 (SPI3) ← pressure ADC │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` ### 1.1 Why three threads? | Thread | Period | Job |--------|--------|-----| Pressure sampling | 1 ms | Match the SSC ASIC's 1 kHz pressure update; produce filtered atomic snapshots that any control loop can consume lock-free. | Valve control | 10 ms | Push every dirty valve setpoint to MAX22200 / TLE92466ED. Doing this at 100 Hz keeps SPI traffic low while still feeling instant to a 500 Hz outer control loop. | Diagnostics | 100 ms | Read per-channel + global driver-IC fault registers and surface a comprehensive `SubsystemFaultSnapshot` so the application doesn't ever have to do multi-register SPI reads itself. | This separation means the control loop **never** has to read fault registers itself — that's the diagnostics thread's responsibility — and the diagnostics thread **never** delays the application's set/get path. --- ## 2. Pressure sensors Honeywell SSC TruStability sensors output **10 % – 90 % of V_supply** over the configured pressure range (transfer function "A"), with output clipping limits at 2.5 % / 97.5 %. Resolution ≥ 0.03 % FSS, accuracy ±0.25 % FSS BFSL, total error band ±2 % FSS, ASIC update ≈ 1 kHz, response ≈ 1 ms. Bench wiring: | Channel | Label | Range | Direction |---------|----------|------------------|------------| CH0 | DPS_LOW | ±0.18 PSI | Differential | CH1 | DPS_HIGH | ±2.32 PSI | Differential | CH2 | PMS | 0 – 5 PSI | Positive | CH3 | PLS_LOW | 0 – 15 PSI | Positive | CH4 | PLS_HIGH | 0 – 150 PSI | Positive | CH5 | RLS | 0 → -30 PSI | Negative (vacuum) | CH6 | PWS2 | 0 – 1 PSI | Positive | CH7 | PWS1 | 0 – 1 PSI | Positive | Pipeline: 1 kHz Auto-1 batched ADS7952 read → per-channel single-pole IIR LPF (default fc = 100 Hz at fs = 1 kHz) → atomic publish. Lock-free `PressureSensor::GetPressureFiltered()` for control loops. --- ## 3. Valves ### 3.1 Driver-IC capabilities (what we expose) #### MAX22200 (octal solenoid driver, 8 channels — using 6) | Capability | Use here |------------|----------| **CDR (Current Drive Regulation)** — 7-bit current ladder per channel | Hit & hold currents on every BinaryHitHold solenoid; sustained current on the SEV pseudo-proportional. | **VDR (Voltage / PWM Duty Regulation)** | Available via `ValveManager::ConfigureSolenoidVdr` — not used today. | **Per-channel feature gates** (CFG_CH register) | All four exposed via `Max22200ChannelFeatures`: `slew_rate_control` (cleaner edges, lower EMI), `open_load_detection`, `plunger_movement_detection`, `hit_current_check`. | **DPM (Detection of Plunger Movement)** — global algorithm (CFG_DPM) | `ManifoldValves::ConfigureGlobalDpm(start_ma, dip_ma, debounce_ms)` configures ISTART / IPTH / TDEB. Per-channel DPM_EN bits set from the catalog's feature gate. | **Per-channel faults** (FAULT register) | `SolenoidValve::Snapshot()` returns `overcurrent`, `hit_not_reached`, `open_load`, `plunger_movement_fault` plus sticky counters. | **Global health** (STATUS register) | `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread::SubsystemFaultSnapshot.max_*` carries OVT, COMER, UVM, the global OCP/OLF/HHF/DPM bits and the active-channels mask. | #### TLE92466ED (six-channel current-controlled, 6 channels — using all 6) | Capability | Use here |------------|----------| **Closed-loop current control** | `ValveManager::SetProportionalCurrent` per valve, called every dirty Apply. | **PWM frequency** (mantissa+exponent encoded) | Each valve's `pwm_hz` from the model spec is pushed once via `ValveManager::ConfigureProportionalPwm`. | **Dither** (step size + steps + flat period) | Pushed once via `ValveManager::ConfigureProportionalDither` for VSO-class valves. LM-Pro skips dither (it's a linear motor). | **Slew rate / diagnostic current / open-load threshold / OLSG warning** | Configured via `tle92466ed::ChannelConfig` from `Tle92466ChannelFeatures`. | **Per-channel diagnostics** | `ProportionalValve::Snapshot()` carries every flag from `tle92466ed::ChannelDiagnostics`: `overcurrent`, `short_to_ground`, `open_load`, `over_temperature`, `open_load_short_ground`, `ot_warning`, `current_regulation_warning`, `pwm_regulation_warning`, `olsg_warning`, plus live measurements `average_current_raw`, `duty_cycle_raw`, `vbat_feedback_raw`. | **Global health** (FaultReport) | `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread::SubsystemFaultSnapshot.tle_*` carries VBAT/VIO/VDD UV/OV, central OT warning/error, clock fault, SPI watchdog, POR/reset events, register/OTP ECC errors, supply-NOK summaries. | ### 3.2 Bench mapping **Solenoids (MAX22200, channels 0–7):** | OUTn | ID | Drive mode | Model | Datasheet currents (24 V) |------------|-------|---------------------|-------------------------------|---------------------------------------| SOL_CH0 | _spare_ | _unconnected_ | — | — | SOL_CH1 | OLV_2 | BinaryHitHold | Parker C21 (R = 235 Ω) | hit 102 mA / hold 51 mA / hit 100 ms | SOL_CH2 | VEV | BinaryHitHold | Parker C15 ≥0.040″ (R = 361 Ω) | hit 66 mA / hold 33 mA / hit 100 ms | SOL_CH3 | OLV_1 | BinaryHitHold | Parker C21 | same as OLV_2 | **SOL_CH4** | **SEV** | **VariableCurrent** | **Parker VSO (R = 274 Ω)** | **0..66 mA proportional via 7-bit CDR ladder** | SOL_CH5 | GDV | BinaryHitHold | Parker SRS 0.5 W (R = 1152 Ω) | hit 21 mA / hold 10 mA / hit 30 ms | SOL_CH6 | ORV | BinaryHitHold | Parker C15 ≥0.040″ | hit 66 mA / hold 33 mA / hit 100 ms | SOL_CH7 | AVV | BinaryHitHold | Parker C15 ≥0.040″ | same as ORV | **Proportionals (TLE92466ED, channels 0–5):** > The TLE92466ED PWM frequency is capped at 4 kHz by the chip itself (datasheet > `PERIOD::kSpecMaxFrequency`). The catalog therefore drives every model at > 4 kHz; the driver clamps and warns if you ever request more. LM-Pro keeps a > tiny "telemetry" dither (1 mA @ 50 Hz) so the chip's `FB_I_AVG` / `FB_DC` > averagers are populated — see `hf-tle92466ed-driver/docs/troubleshooting.md`. | OUTn | ID | Model | Full-flow current | PWM | Dither |-----------|-------|-----------------------------|-------------------|---------|----------------------| PROP_CH0 | FRV | Parker VSO MaxFlow 24 V | 66 mA | 4 kHz | 4 mA @ 200 Hz | PROP_CH1 | SPV_L | Parker VSO 24 V | 66 mA | 4 kHz | 4 mA @ 200 Hz | PROP_CH2 | FCV | Parker VSO MaxFlow 24 V | 66 mA | 4 kHz | 4 mA @ 200 Hz | PROP_CH3 | LSV | Parker VSO MaxFlow 24 V | 66 mA | 4 kHz | 4 mA @ 200 Hz | PROP_CH4 | SPV_H | Parker LM-Pro 24 V | 115 mA | 4 kHz | 1 mA @ 50 Hz (telemetry) | PROP_CH5 | GFV | Parker LM-Pro 24 V | 115 mA | 4 kHz | 1 mA @ 50 Hz (telemetry) | ### 3.3 SEV — pseudo-proportional via MAX22200 SEV is a Parker VSO proportional valve, but because precise control is not required at this site we route it through MAX22200 instead of taking up a TLE92466ED channel. The driver mode is `VariableCurrent`: - Every Apply() pushes `ConfigureSolenoidCdr(target_ma, target_ma, hit_time = 0)`. - With `hit_time = 0` the MAX22200 skips the hit phase; the channel runs at a steady current equal to the requested setpoint. - Resolution is 7-bit (≈ 128 steps over 0..IFS); for SEV's 0..66 mA range that's ~0.5 mA per step — more than enough for opening-percentage control. - DPM and HHF are disabled for SEV (no hit phase to check; the dip signature DPM looks for is for binary on/off solenoids). ### 3.4 Per-valve atomic state (`Valve.h`) Every valve carries: ```text target_pos_ atomic — last setpoint requested (0..1) target_dirty_ atomic — pending application? actual_pos_ atomic — last position the control thread set state_ atomic— Idle / Active / Faulted / … last_error_ atomic apply_count_ atomic apply_error_count_ atomic fault_count_ atomic last_fault_tick_ms_ atomic ``` All `Get*` accessors use `memory_order_acquire`; the control / diagnostics threads use `memory_order_release` on their writes. A single load yields a self-consistent snapshot — control loops never need a mutex. ### 3.5 Application API ```cpp auto& sys = manifold_valves::ManifoldValves::GetInstance(); // Binary solenoid: sys.Get(manifold_valves::SolenoidId::OLV_1).RequestState(true); bool actual_on = sys.Get(manifold_valves::SolenoidId::OLV_1).IsActuallyEnergised(); // Pseudo-proportional solenoid (SEV via MAX22200 CDR): sys.Get(manifold_valves::SolenoidId::SEV).RequestPosition(0.42f); // 0..1 // Precision proportional (TLE92466ED): sys.Get(manifold_valves::ProportionalId::FCV).RequestPosition(0.42f); float actual = sys.Get(manifold_valves::ProportionalId::FCV).GetActualPosition(); // Per-valve diagnostic snapshot: auto sol_snap = sys.Get(manifold_valves::SolenoidId::OLV_1).Snapshot(); if (sol_snap.plunger_movement_fault) { /* handle stuck valve */ } auto pro_snap = sys.Get(manifold_valves::ProportionalId::FCV).Snapshot(); uint16_t avg_current = pro_snap.average_current_raw; // live measured // Subsystem-wide health (run by ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread): auto sub = valve_diag.GetSnapshot(); if (sub.tle_vbat_uv || sub.max_undervoltage) { /* supply problem */ } ``` All `Request*` and `Get*` calls are lock-free. The actual SPI traffic happens on the next iteration of the control / diagnostics threads. --- ## 4. Diagnostics for medical-device safety The diagnostics thread surfaces every flag the chip can publish — not just "any fault" booleans. This is what allows the application layer to make informed safety decisions: ### 4.1 Active diagnostics — react in software | Signal | Meaning | Recommended response |--------|---------|----------------------| `Solenoid.plunger_movement_fault` | Plunger did not move under load | Mark valve mechanically stuck; alarm; safe-state the system. | `Solenoid.hit_not_reached` | HIT current never achieved within tHIT | Coil drift, supply sag or open coil. Re-attempt; alarm if persistent. | `Solenoid.open_load` | No load current path | Disconnected coil or wire. Disable channel, alarm. | `Solenoid.overcurrent` | Short to supply or shorted coil | Disable immediately; latch. | `Proportional.short_to_ground` | Short to ground | Latched fault. | `Proportional.over_temperature` | Channel die over-temp | Reduce setpoint; back-off duty; alarm. | `Proportional.current_regulation_warning` | Loop can't track current setpoint | Investigate wiring, supply, dither tuning. | `Subsystem.tle_vbat_uv` / `_ov` | Supply rail UV/OV | Stop actuating; raise system alarm. | `Subsystem.tle_spi_wd_error` | SPI watchdog tripped | Communication is failing; latch and re-init. | `Subsystem.tle_reg_ecc_err` / `tle_otp_ecc_err` | Register / OTP memory error | Treat as hard failure; latch. | `Subsystem.max_undervoltage` (UVM) | MAX22200 supply UV at boot or runtime | Re-read STATUS at init clears it; runtime UV is an alarm. | `Subsystem.max_communication_error` | SPI error detected by MAX22200 | Re-init; alarm if persistent. | ### 4.2 Preventive features (configured at startup) - **Slew-rate control** enabled by default on every solenoid → cleaner switching edges, lower EMI, less acoustic clicking. - **Open-load detection** enabled on every channel → catches a disconnected coil before it hides a real safety event. - **Hit-current check (HHF)** enabled on every binary solenoid → if the hit current isn't reached within tHIT we know the solenoid never energised. - **DPM (plunger movement)** enabled on all 5 binary cartridge solenoids. Tuned via `ConfigureGlobalDpm(30 mA, 8 mA, 0.5 ms)` at boot — adjust per the actual mechanical signature. - **OLSG warning** on every TLE92466 channel → early indication of open-load / short-to-ground precursors. - **CRC + SPI watchdog + clock watchdog** on TLE92466ED globally (configured by `Flux::ValveManager` on init). --- ## 5. Failure / degraded-mode behaviour If `Flux::ValveManager` fails to bring up either driver IC (the WH bench in its current state shows exactly this — the hardware isn't connected): - `ValveManager::IsInitialized()` returns `false`. - `ManifoldValvesControlThread` keeps stepping but skips `Apply()` calls. - `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread` reports `manager_ready = false` and zeroes the per-driver readiness flags / fault snapshots. - All `Valve::Get*` accessors keep returning the last-published soft state (`Uninitialized` / 0 / `VALVE_SUCCESS`). This means an outer control loop can be developed and unit-tested against the same atomic API even when the valve hardware isn't wired up. --- ## 6. Boot self-test (`ManifoldValvesSelfTest`) Every boot, after the pressure thread is calibrated and the valve control + diagnostics threads are running, the application calls `ManifoldValvesSelfTest::Run()`. This single function: 1. **Walks every solenoid in the catalog** (`SolenoidId::OLV_2 → AVV`) and: - Prints a banner ("Connect ONLY SOL '' …") with a configurable prompt countdown so the operator can move the manifold tube. - Cycles the channel `solenoid_cycles` × (ON `solenoid_on_ms` / OFF `solenoid_off_ms`) — exact same test pattern as the `c21_cycle_test.cpp` example in the MAX22200 driver. - After each ON/OFF transition waits two full diagnostics-thread sweeps and logs a per-channel snapshot (`tgt`, `act`, state, OCP / HHF / OLF / DPM flags, sticky `fc`). 2. **Walks every proportional in the catalog** (`ProportionalId::FRV → GFV`) and: - Prompts the operator (same pattern). - Ramps `0 → full-flow → 0` in `proportional_steps` increments with a `proportional_settle_ms` settle between each setpoint — same pattern as the `lm_pro_cycle_test.cpp` example in the TLE92466ED driver. - Logs the chip's live telemetry at every step: commanded current, `FB_I_AVG` raw, `FB_DC` raw, `last_err`, every fault flag and every warning. 3. **Aggregates a per-valve PASS/FAIL** based on: - `apply_error_count_` delta (ANY non-success Apply during the cycle). - `fault_count_` delta (any per-channel fault flag set during the cycle). - The most recent diagnostic snapshot (`Snapshot::any_fault()`). The summary block at the end prints OK / FAIL plus a one-line fault description for each valve. ### 6.1 Operator workflow on a manifold-limited rig The bench can only mechanically attach **one valve to the manifold at a time**. The defaults (`prompt_wait_ms = 3000`, `inter_valve_pause_ms = 4000`) are tuned for that workflow: | Phase | Duration |---------------------------------|----------| Per-valve operator prompt | 3 s | Per-valve test (solenoid) | ~12 s (3 × on/off cycles) | Per-valve test (proportional) | ~5 s (22 ramp setpoints × 0.15 s) | Pause between valves | 4 s | **Full sweep** (7 sol + 6 prop) | **≈ 3 min** | Tweak the constants in `MakeSelfTestPlan()` at the top of `manifold_valves_pressure_control.cpp` to: - skip valves that are not yet stocked (set the `enable_*` flag to `false`); - shorten / lengthen the pulse profiles or ramp resolution; - disable the operator prompt (`prompt_wait_ms = 0`) for fully unattended runs. To skip the self-test entirely set `kRunSelfTestAtBoot = false` at the top of the same file. ### 6.2 What the self-test catches The self-test is the cheapest way to **catch a stuck plunger, an unconnected coil, a damaged driver IC, or an audibly dead solenoid** before the rig starts running pressure-control loops. Specifically: | Symptom | Catalog check that surfaces it |------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------| Coil disconnected / connector reversed | `open_load` / `open_load_short_ground` flag, `last_err = "Open load detected"` | Coil shorted to GND | `short_to_ground` flag (TLE92466ED) | Plunger stuck in valve seat | `plunger_movement_fault` (MAX22200 DPM) | Solenoid hit current never reached | `hit_not_reached` (MAX22200 HHF) | TLE chip not in correct mode | `last_err = "Operation not allowed in mode"` (Apply-time error count) | Supply browning out | `SubsystemFaultSnapshot.max_undervoltage` / `tle_vbat_uv` | TLE PWM regulation can't track | `pwm_regulation_warning` | TLE current loop can't track | `current_regulation_warning` | Over-temperature, ECC error | `over_temperature` / `ot_warning` / `tle_reg_ecc_err` | > ⚠️ **Configuration-Mode round-trip:** Each `ProportionalValve` enters > Configuration Mode, pushes its `ChannelConfig` + PWM + dither, then > re-enters Mission Mode. This is required because the TLE92466ED rejects > any `CH_x_CTRL` write while in Mission Mode and the handler enters > Mission Mode at init time. Skipping this round-trip is what produced the > infamous "every Apply returns Operation-not-allowed-in-mode" symptom. --- ## 7. Extension recipes ### 6.1 Add a binary solenoid 1. Add an enumerator in `manifold_valves::SolenoidId` before `Count`. 2. Append a row in `kSolenoidMap` referencing one of the `kSpec*` model structs and an unused `ValveChannel::SOL_CHn`. ### 6.2 Add a pseudo-proportional via MAX22200 Same as above, but: - pick `SolenoidDriveMode::VariableCurrent`, - use a model spec with `full_flow_current_ma` set and `hit_current_ma = hold_current_ma = 0`, - disable `plunger_movement_detection` and `hit_current_check` in the channel features (the current waveform in continuous-current mode is not what those algorithms were designed for). ### 6.3 Add a precision proportional 1. Add an enumerator in `manifold_valves::ProportionalId` before `Count` (TLE92466 has 6 channels — if you exceed that you need a second IC). 2. Append a row in `kProportionalMap` with the right model spec and feature gates. ### 6.4 Use a different model Edit (or add) a `SolenoidModelSpec` / `ProportionalModelSpec` literal at the top of `ManifoldValvesCatalog.h`, then point the relevant table row at it. Only the catalog file changes. ### 6.5 Re-tune diagnostics - DPM parameters: `ManifoldValves::ConfigureGlobalDpm(start, dip, debounce)`. Default 30 mA / 8 mA / 0.5 ms tuned for the C21 hold band; adjust per the actual mechanical signature. - Per-channel feature gates: edit the `Max22200ChannelFeatures` / `Tle92466ChannelFeatures` row in the bench map. - Diagnostics thread cadence: `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread::SetPeriodMs(n)` — default 100 ms, drop to 20 ms for closer monitoring or raise to 500 ms to lighten SPI load. --- ## 8. Files in this folder | File | Purpose |------|---------| `manifold_valves_pressure_control.cpp` | App entry: brings up Flux, calibrates pressure sensors, configures DPM, starts control + diagnostics threads. | `PressureSensorConfig.h` | Sensor enums + ratiometric range + calibration config types. | `PressureSensor.{h,cpp}` | Per-channel pressure sensor: IIR filter, atomic publish. | `PressureSensorThread.{h,cpp}` | 1 kHz BaseThread + Auto-1 ADS7952 batch read. | `ManifoldValvesCatalog.h` | Compile-time enums + Parker valve datasheet specs + bench map + per-channel diagnostic feature gates. | `Valve.h` | Base valve class (atomic state, dirty flag, snapshot types). | `SolenoidValve.h` | MAX22200-driven valve — handles BinaryHitHold and VariableCurrent modes; decodes per-channel OCP/HHF/OLF/DPM. | `ProportionalValve.h` | TLE92466ED-driven precision proportional; full per-channel ChannelDiagnostics surfacing. | `ManifoldValves.h` | Singleton container, O(1) lookup, iteration helpers, `ConfigureGlobalDpm`. | `ManifoldValvesControlThread.h` | 100 Hz BaseThread that pushes dirty setpoints. | `ManifoldValvesDiagnosticsThread.h` | 10 Hz BaseThread; per-valve + per-driver-IC fault decoding into `SubsystemFaultSnapshot`. | `ManifoldValvesSelfTest.h` | Boot-time per-valve cycler — solenoid ON/OFF and proportional 0→full→0 ramps with full diagnostic capture. Header-only; configured from `MakeSelfTestPlan()` in the app entry. | `README.md` | This document. |

# Flux API — Unified HardFOC Platform Interface ## CPU affinity (`FluxCpuAffinity.h`) FreeRTOS task pinning uses **logical** core indices defined in `FluxCpuAffinity.h` (`flux_hal::kFluxCpuNoAffinity`, `kFluxCpuHostIo`, `kFluxCpuRealtime`). Application firmware (`main/`) includes that header only—vendor core names (e.g. PRO/APP on Espressif dual-core parts) are documented in the board integration guide, not as macros in `main/`. ## Overview The Flux API provides a unified singleton interface to all component managers in the HardFOC Flux V1 platform. It implements lazy initialization with proper dependency management, ensuring all subsystems are correctly initialized before exposing them to the application. ## Architecture ### Design Principles - **True Singleton Pattern**: Uses Meyer's singleton for thread-safe initialization - **Lazy Initialization**: Components are initialized only when needed - **Dependency Management**: Proper initialization order based on component dependencies - **Exception-Free Design**: All methods are `noexcept` with proper error handling - **Reference-Based Access**: Direct access to component managers by reference - **Comprehensive Diagnostics**: Full system health monitoring and diagnostics ### Component Dependencies The initialization order is carefully managed to handle dependencies: ``` 1. NvsManager (ESP-IDF NVS — `flux` / `flux_cal` / `flux_cfg` namespaces) ↓ 2. CommChannelsManager (SPI, CAN, lazy UART, opt-in USB Serial/JTAG — no I²C on Flux V1) ↓ 3. GpioManager (depends on comms for future expansion) ↓ 4. ValveManager (depends on comms + gpio for drivers) ↓ 5. AdcManager (ESP32 internal ADC, independent) ↓ 6. LedManager (WS2812, independent) ↓ 7. TemperatureManager (depends on ADC) ``` > **Logger backend.** `Flux::EnsureInitialized()` (and the constructor's > early `Logger::GetInstance().Initialize()` call) use the **default** > `Logger::Initialize(const LogConfig&)` overload, which delegates to the > per-MCU factory `Logger::CreateDefaultBaseLogger()`. On ESP32 builds > that factory lives in `hf-core/handlers/logger/factory/EspLoggerFactory.cpp` > and returns an `EspLogger` — so `Logger.cpp` itself never includes any > ESP-IDF headers. To inject a custom backend (e.g. one that writes over > `EspUsbSerialJtag` instead of UART0), call the second `Initialize` > overload **before** `Flux::EnsureInitialized()`. See the > [`Logger` handler README](../core/handlers/logger/README.md). ## Quick Start ### Basic Usage ```cpp #include "api/Flux.h" #include "core/hf-core-drivers/internal/hf-internal-interface-wrap/inc/base/BaseNvs.h" // Get the Flux API instance auto& flux = Flux::GetInstance(); // Ensure all systems are initialized if (flux.EnsureInitialized()) { // Non-volatile storage (BaseNvs — calibration, config, app keys) BaseNvs& cal = flux.nvs.Calibration(); (void)cal.KeyExists("my_cal_key"); // Access communication channels auto& comms = flux.comms; // Access GPIO management auto& gpio = flux.gpio; // Access valve control auto& valves = flux.valves; // Access ADC channels auto& adc = flux.adc; // Access LED management auto& leds = flux.leds; // Access temperature sensors auto& temp = flux.temp; } ``` ### String-Based Access (Convenience) ```cpp auto& flux = Flux::GetInstance(); if (flux.EnsureInitialized()) { // GPIO operations flux.gpio.Set("GPIO_MAX22200_FAULT", true); bool state; flux.gpio.Read("GPIO_TLE_DIAG", state); // ADC operations float voltage; flux.adc.ReadVoltage("ADC_NTC_THERM", voltage); // Valve control flux.valves.EnableChannel(ValveChannel::SOL_CH0); // LED status flux.leds.SetStatus(LedAnimation::STATUS_OK); } ``` ### Cached Access (High Performance) ```cpp auto& flux = Flux::GetInstance(); if (flux.EnsureInitialized()) { // Cache pointers for fast access (do once, outside loops) auto* adc_ntc = flux.adc.Get("ADC_NTC_THERM"); auto* adc_vbus = flux.adc.Get("ADC_VBUS_MONITOR"); if (!adc_ntc || !adc_vbus) { printf("ERROR: Failed to cache component pointers
"); return; } // Use cached pointers in high-frequency operations for (int i = 0; i ReadChannelV(0, ntc_v); adc_vbus->ReadChannelV(0, vbus_v); } } ``` ### Advanced Usage ```cpp // Get system diagnostics FluxSystemDiagnostics diagnostics; if (flux.GetSystemDiagnostics(diagnostics)) { printf("System Health: %s
", diagnostics.system_healthy ? "HEALTHY" : "UNHEALTHY"); printf("Initialized Components: %u/%u
", diagnostics.initialized_components, diagnostics.total_components); } // Collect per-manager health ManagerHealthSnapshot snapshot; if (flux.CollectManagerHealth(snapshot)) { for (size_t i = 0; i GetComponentInitializationStatus() const noexcept; size_t GetFailedComponents(const char* out[], size_t max_count) const noexcept; size_t GetSystemWarnings(const char* out[], size_t max_count) const noexcept; bool CollectManagerHealth(ManagerHealthSnapshot& snapshot) noexcept; ``` ### Utility Methods ```cpp uint64_t GetSystemUptimeMs() const noexcept; uint64_t GetInitializationTimeMs() const noexcept; void DumpSystemStatistics() const noexcept; bool PerformHealthCheck() noexcept; const char* GetSystemVersion() const noexcept; ``` ### Convenience Accessor ```cpp [[nodiscard]] inline Flux& GetFlux() noexcept; ``` Equivalent to `Flux::GetInstance()`. ### Macros ```cpp #define FLUX_API Flux::GetInstance() #define FLUX_API_INIT() (Flux::GetInstance().EnsureInitialized(), Flux::GetInstance()) ``` ## System Diagnostics ### FluxSystemDiagnostics ```cpp struct FluxSystemDiagnostics { bool system_healthy; bool nvs_initialized; bool comms_initialized; bool gpio_initialized; bool valves_initialized; bool adc_initialized; bool leds_initialized; bool temp_initialized; uint32_t total_components; // equals kFluxManagerCount (7) uint32_t initialized_components; uint32_t failed_components; uint64_t initialization_time_ms; uint64_t system_uptime_ms; const char* failed_components_list[kFluxManagerCount]; size_t failed_components_list_count; }; ``` ### ManagerHealthSnapshot ```cpp struct ManagerHealthSnapshot { ManagerHealthEntry entries[kFluxManagerCount]; size_t count; size_t managers_with_errors; bool all_healthy; }; ``` ## Performance ### Initialization Time - **Fast Path**: ~30–80 ms (all components healthy) - **Slow Path**: ~150–400 ms (with retries and error handling) ### Memory Usage - **Static Memory**: ~1.5 KB (singleton instance) - **Runtime Memory**: ~0.5 KB (diagnostics and state tracking) - **Component Memory**: Varies by component (not owned by API) ### Thread Safety - **Singleton Access**: Thread-safe (Meyer's singleton) - **Initialization**: Thread-safe with atomic operations - **Component Access**: Depends on individual component implementations ## NVS example (ESP32-S3) See `examples/esp32/main/flux_nvs_example.cpp` — build and flash with: `./scripts/build_app.sh flux_nvs_example Debug` then `./scripts/flash_app.sh flash_monitor flux_nvs_example Debug` from `examples/esp32/`. ## Related documentation - [HAL documentation hub](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/docs/hal/README.html) - [Manager ↔ handler map](/hf-hal-flux-v1/development/docs/hal/managers-and-handlers.html) - Manager headers: [`../../lib/managers/`](../../lib/managers/)
